articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activities calendar for March and April, including observational astronomy classes, numerous star parties at various locations, and general meetings. It also reports on the January 1999 general meeting where Jay Freeman was honored with the A. B. Gregory Award for his contributions to amateur astronomy and subsequently delivered a talk on deep-sky observing with small telescopes.

articles.title: Twin "Blue Moons" in 1999
articles.summary: The article discusses the rare occurrence of "blue moons," defined as two full moons in a single calendar month, highlighting 1999 as a year featuring twin blue moons in January and March. This phenomenon, along with February having no full moon, is noted for its rarity, making 1999 only the third time this century such a pattern occurred, last seen in 1961 and 1915. The article also touches upon the cyclical nature of blue moons and their historical patterns.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article, 'Mooning,' highlights March as an optimal time for lunar observation due to the Moon's high elevation at first quarter, which provides clearer views. It offers a detailed guide for observing specific lunar features on March 22nd and 23rd, including prominent craters like Aristotle and Eudoxis, various rilles such as Hyginus and Triesnecker, and geological formations like the Alpine Valley and Altai Scarp, providing targets for both casual and dedicated observers.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: The article "COMET COMMENTS" by Don Machholz provides updates on several comets, including Comet Linear, Comet Williams, and Periodic Comets Jager and Harrington-Abell. A primary focus is the visual discovery of Comet Tilbrook (C/1998 A1) by Australian amateur astronomer Justin Tilbrook, detailing its discovery circumstances and subsequent dimming. The author also highlights recent trends in visual comet discoveries, noting a prevalence of finds by Southern Hemisphere observers, particularly from Australia.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES - Epoch 2000, 0h UT
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for three comets: C/1998 M5 (LINEAR), C/1998 P1 (Williams), and P/1998 U3 (Jager). For each comet, it details their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation, and predicted sky magnitude for various dates between February and April, all referenced to Epoch 2000, 0h UT. This data is essential for tracking and observing these specific comets.

articles.title: ELEMENTS
articles.summary: This document, titled 'ELEMENTS', provides detailed orbital elements for several celestial objects, including Williams, LINEAR (M5), Harrington-Abell, and Jager, with references to MPEC and MPC circulars. It also includes an observational ephemeris for comet 52P/Harrington-Abell, listing its predicted right ascension, declination, and sky magnitude for various dates in early 1999.

articles.title: Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for March 1999, with a strong focus on lunar features and Mars. For the Moon, it highlights specific rilles, craters like Plato, Copernicus, and Clavius, and "catenae" to observe around the first quarter, offering tips for specific dates. It also advises starting Mars observation early in anticipation of its April 24 opposition, recommending practice to discern subtle features such as polar caps, Syrtis Major, and suggesting the use of sketches and filters.

articles.title: Andrah Foundation Supports Loaner Program
articles.summary: The Andrah Foundation, a charitable organization founded by Ruth S. Knoll and Thomas Knoll, with recent contributions directed by Paul and Ann Summers, has donated $250. This gift is intended to support community activities that promote astronomy awareness and interest, specifically recommending its use for the Telescope Loaner Program. The article also provides a guide for observing Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto in the March sky.

articles.title: A.S.P. Seeks Project ASTRO Volunteers
articles.summary: The article details two distinct astronomy initiatives: the Astronomical Society of the Pacific (ASP) is seeking amateur and professional astronomers for Project ASTRO to partner with 4th-9th grade teachers in Bay Area schools for hands-on science education. Separately, the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting a "Weekly Grind" workshop at Houge Park, where members, guided by experts like Jane Houston, are actively engaged in grinding their own telescope mirrors.

articles.title: LUNAR PHASES (Dates PST):
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed schedule of lunar phases for a specific month, listing the exact times and dates (PST) for Full Moon, Last Quarter, New Moon, and First Quarter. For each phase, it also includes the moon's rise, transit, and set times, offering comprehensive information for tracking lunar cycles.

articles.title: NEARER PLANETS:
articles.summary: This document presents an astronomical ephemeris for five 'nearer planets'—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—across three specific dates. For each planet and date, it provides detailed observational data including rise, transit, and set times, Right Ascension, Declination, distance in Astronomical Units (A.U.), and visual magnitude, serving as a comprehensive guide for planetary observers.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System?
articles.summary: This article, titled "SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System?", raises a speculative question about the potential for intelligent life to exist within a G2V star system, which is the classification for our Sun. It includes a table presenting astronomical data such as rise, transit, and set times, along with right ascension and declination coordinates for various dates. The specific connection between these observational data points and the central question of intelligent life is not elaborated in the provided content.

articles.title: ASTRONOMICAL TWILIGHT:
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing the beginning and end times of astronomical twilight for several specific dates, identified by Julian Date. It provides precise time data, likely intended for astronomical planning or determining optimal observing windows. The information helps users understand the duration of astronomical twilight on those particular days.

articles.title: SIDEREAL TIME:
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing sidereal time values for specific dates (the 7th, 17th, and 27th), showing the right ascension transiting at local midnight. It serves as a reference for calculating or understanding sidereal time at given moments.

articles.title: DARKEST SATURDAY NIGHT:
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical twilight times for March 13, 1999, titled "DARKEST SATURDAY NIGHT." It details specific timings for sunset, the end of astronomical twilight, moonrise, and the beginning of dawn, culminating in a calculated duration of 9 hours and 15 minutes of darkness.

articles.title: Y2K strikes the SJAA!
articles.summary: The SJAA's eleven-inch Compustar telescope is experiencing a Y2K problem, as its date entry system assumes years in the 1900s and cannot accept '00' for 2000. A workaround involves entering a date four years prior, which allows the scope to correctly polar align and go to designated objects. This issue affects club equipment that was once a groundbreaking demonstration.

articles.title: The Chronicle of a Net Community 26 Jan 1999
articles.summary: This article chronicles a real-time online discussion among amateur astronomers on January 26, 1999, as they attempt to observe lunar occultations. Participants share their experiences and sightings of stars like Aldebaran and other Hyades members from various Bay Area locations, despite challenges like cloudy weather or a bright moon. The exchanges capture their enthusiasm for witnessing these celestial events.

articles.title: January 30, 1999
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association's January 30, 1999, meeting covered operational and administrative matters. Discussions included implementing hosts for dark sky parties, encouraging donations for loaner scopes, and successfully raising over $400 through APD sales. Key administrative decisions involved establishing a club PO box and electing an AANC representative, while the urgent need for a club treasurer was also highlighted.

articles.title: A One-Day Workshop on Saturday March 27, 1999 in the May Treat Morrison Auditorium and Morrison Planetarium
articles.summary: The article primarily details a one-day astronomy workshop held on Saturday, March 27, 1999, at the Morrison Planetarium, featuring prominent speakers discussing topics such as the future of the universe, lunar and Mars exploration, exoplanets, and SETI. Additionally, it includes a collection of informal, timestamped observing reports from several individuals sharing their real-time experiences of an Aldebaran occultation.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors for an organization, detailing their positions such as President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and Director. Each entry includes the individual's name and contact phone number, providing a clear directory of the organization's leadership.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document, titled "Ephemeris Staff," lists the key personnel involved with the Ephemeris publication along with their respective phone numbers. It identifies the Editors (Jane Houston and Morris Jones), Circulation staff (Bob Brauer and Lew Kurtz), and the printing service (Accuprint).

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Ephemeris encourages its members to submit articles for publication. Submissions should be sent directly to the editors via email at ephemeris@whiteoaks.com.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: All San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner scopes are currently available for members to borrow. Members interested in utilizing this service should contact Mike Koop via email or phone at the provided work or home numbers.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) maintains a list of telescopes, referred to as "Stored Scopes," which are available for immediate loan to its members. These scopes are kept at various members' homes, and interested borrowers can arrange pickup by contacting Mike Koop at any SJAA event.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes that are currently on loan, specifying each scope's description, the borrower, and its due date. It also informs potential borrowers that they can be placed on a waiting list for a scope to become available.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes that have had their loan periods extended, making them available for potential transfer to new borrowers. Individuals interested in borrowing one of these scopes can contact the organization to arrange a transfer with the current borrower. The list includes various telescope types, current borrowers, due dates, and specific notes regarding contact or indefinite loan periods.

articles.title: Waiting List:
articles.summary: This document presents a waiting list or equipment borrowing record, detailing specific astronomical scopes and their current or requested borrowers. It includes entries for a Solar Scope borrowed by Dave North and a Newtonian scope requested by Darryl Lambert.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The 'SJAA Ephemeris,' the San Jose Astronomical Association's official newsletter, is published monthly, totaling 12 issues per year, from January through December. The statement also provides the association's mailing address.

articles.title: To subscribe to or unsubscribe from the SJAA Mailing List send email to:
articles.summary: This document provides instructions on how to subscribe to or unsubscribe from the SJAA Mailing List. Users need to send an email to sjaa-request@seds.org with a blank subject line and a single text line containing either 'subscribe' or 'unsubscribe'. This information was published in the SJAA Ephemeris, March 1999.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships at standard ($15) and junior ($6) rates. It also offers an optional Sky & Telescope magazine subscription for an additional $27. Instructions for submitting the form and payment (checks payable to SJAA) are provided, along with contact details for the treasurer and the association's mailing address.
